architecturalPlan.scaleRationale: A compact two-storey residence keeps the enclosed footprint within the narrow 8 metre lot while reserving a meaningful rear garden and pool court; the three-bedroom requirement is allocated to the upper private envelope rather than inferred as fitted rooms. Price and site depth were not supplied, so the scale is an architectural capacity assumption rather than a budget-derived area calculation.
architecturalPlan.arrivalAndCirculation: The ground slab walking datum is 0.15 m and receives a covered front approach at the same datum; a real recessed entrance opens into the public lower envelope. A 18-riser straight stair rises 3.45 m from the ground floor datum to the 3.60 m upper-floor datum through a reserved slab void, providing actual access to the private upper accommodation; service and room subdivision are deferred.
architecturalPlan.volumeHierarchy: The principal volume is a 7.0 by 10.0 m, 3.20 m-high lower living envelope, while a 6.30 by 5.70 m upper private volume is recessed within its roof line from 3.60 m to 6.60 m. Flat lower roof strips deliberately surround the upper footprint without crossing it, and the upper roof is a thin, deep-edged horizontal datum at 6.60 m.
architecturalPlan.relationshipsAndViews: Arrival occurs from the south through a shaded threshold, with the long lower volume leading to a fully glazed rear garden opening. A rear terrace connects directly to the pool’s near dry deck at the shared 0.15 m datum; the pool and garden reserve remain beyond the house, and side openings bring daylight into the narrow side clearances.
architecturalPlan.roofFacadeAndMaterials: Ivory rendered planes, limestone horizontal roofs and bronze-framed glazing form a restrained modern palette, with timber used only for the sheltered entry screen and threshold emphasis. Ground-level living glazing is broad and recessed under roof strips, upper bedroom glazing is more measured for privacy, and the entry canopy projects from a developed front elevation on explicit bronze posts.
